learning_outcomes.text: The student becomes familiar with the operational amplifier, its characteristics, various circuits and applications.
The student will be able to recognize the different basic circuits, explain their operation and calculate the different components.
The student learns to apply the theoretical material covered in the exercises.
The student learns to use simulation models and software and can interpret the results.
The student can solve a problem using the theory. Problems arising during the setup of the circuit can be explained and solved by the student's reasoning.
The student will be able to search for information that can help him with the lab assignments.
The student correctly interprets the (measurement) results and calculations of the assignments.
The student can evaluate his measurement results and compare them with theoretical calculations and simulations and draw conclusions from them.
Students work in small groups and the lab assignments can be considered as small-scale projects.
The student will verbally communicate solutions and problems, both with fellow students, lecturers, and other interested parties.
Students work on assignments in pairs. They both search for solutions and make the choice together.
To solve problems that arise during the setup of the analog circuit, an appropriate solution strategy is necessary.
The student has knowledge of basic analog electronics.
The student can look up component data on the internet and also interpret and use it in the circuits being built.

syllabus_topics: The ideal op-amp: basic circuits and properties
Difference and instrumentation amplifier and applications
The ideal op-amp: basic circuits and properties

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam with written preparation (theory + exercises)
Points achieved based on demonstrated assignments during the semester (lab)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on the theory + exercises (100%) and lab (100%). For the first examination opportunity, the theory + exercises component is an oral exam with written preparation. The lab component is based on points achieved from demonstrated assignments during the semester. For the second examination opportunity, both theory + exercises and lab are oral exams with written preparation, with the lab requiring prior preparation of a work piece and demonstration of a practical assignment. Partial transfers are possible for successful partial results (YT5915, YT5916) within the academic year.
